name: BEFORE & AFTER
scope: Every answer is two known things run together on a word they share — the last word of the first is the first word of the second.

clues.q: Gotham's caped pair, joined to the outlaw of Sherwood Forest
The boy wizard of Hogwarts, joined to the spinning disc a pot is thrown on
The clown who sells hamburgers, joined to the fortieth president
The liner that went down in 1912, joined to a warship's wall of steel
The boundary a black hole allows nothing back across, joined to the formal dance

name: POTPOURRI
scope: Every answer is an ordinary household object. The subjects roam; the answers never leave the house.

clues.q: An everyday thing with a head and teeth and no mouth at all
This cooking vessel takes its name by a long road from the Latin scutella, a little dish
David Smith patented the spring-loaded version of this fastener in 1853
Long before synthetic ones, a dried gourd did this bathroom job
Melville Bissell patented a mechanical one of these in 1876, to get sawdust out of a shop floor

name: WORD ORIGINS
scope: Every answer is where an English word came from — the language it was borrowed out of, or the place or person behind it.

clues.q: Kindergarten arrives in English straight from this language, meaning a garden of children
Sabotage comes from this language's word for a wooden shoe
Assassin traces back to a secretive eleventh-century sect in what is now this country
The name of the citrus fruit reached English from naranj, a word in this language
Shrapnel is named for a gunnery officer who served this country's army
